item.title: MercoPress: Chile reinforcing its military presence in Magallanes Region and Antarctica
item.description: Chile announced the reinforcement of its military capacities in the Magallanes Region, extreme south of the country with a plan that includes renewal of aircraft, modernization of armored vehicles, increased vigilance and presence in the austral territory and Antarctica, updating of military strategy based on experiences from the current war scenarios in Europe and Middle East.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands at Labour Conference in Liverpool
item.description: British political parties are holding their annual round of conferences and Labour, in government, has chosen the city of Liverpool for a gathering that started on Sunday, 27 September and will last for three days until 30th September.

item.title: MercoPress: The Telegraph links the Chagos deal to Argentina's Falklands campaign
item.description: An opinion column published on Sunday in the British newspaper The Telegraph argues that the decision to transfer sovereignty over the Chagos Islands to Mauritius served as a signal of weakness that encouraged claims over other British overseas territories, among them the Falklands. The piece, by journalist Daniel Johnson, is an argument of opinion rather than a report of new facts.

item.title: MercoPress: Britain has just received a painful reminder that nobody respects weakness
item.description: By Daniel Hannan (*) As the Chagos humiliation shows, the Foreign Office’s slavish adoration of international courts has got us nowhere. What has all our imagined soft power brought us? For all our performative internationalism, we find ourselves friendless.

item.title: MercoPress: London says Argentina “lacks the ability” to take the Falklands
item.description: British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said Argentina “lacks the ability” to take the Falkland Islands and that the United Kingdom “has the ability to defend” them, in an interview with the Sunday paper The Sun on Sunday published on Saturday. Asked whether London could protect the archipelago militarily if Buenos Aires sent warships, he answered yes.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Brazil's Lula bans online gambling ahead of presidential election
item.description: Lula, who is currently in a tight presidential race against Flávio Bolsonaro, said the industry was a "cancer" that he must "remove".

item.title: BBC Latin America: Venezuela releases dozens of political prisoners as election calls grow
item.description: A slew of dissidents being released from long-term detention comes days after the nation's interim leader met the US president.

item.title: MercoPress: Brazil reaches the election with its top court under suspicion and the candidates tied
item.description: Brazil votes next Sunday in a presidential election that arrives with the Supreme Federal Court mired in its worst institutional crisis since the return to democracy, the right's candidate formally under investigation in the same case, and the two leading contenders tied within the margin of error in every poll.

item.title: MercoPress: De la Espriella announces the reopening of oil exploration in Colombia, including fracking
item.description: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella announced on Friday that his government will "fully" reopen hydrocarbon exploration and the signing of new contracts, including hydraulic fracturing, during the swearing-in of businessman Joaquín Gutiérrez as president of Ecopetrol, the country's largest company.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands Assembly responds to Argentina's campaign: “This Assembly remains calm”
item.description: The chair of the Falkland Islands Legislative Assembly, Jack Ford, said on Thursday during a sitting of the body that there is “nothing new” in the claims made this week, and that the institution “remains calm” and steadfast in defending the right of the archipelago's residents to determine their own future.

item.title: MercoPress: The Falklands economic development agency appoints Josh Smith as managing director
item.description: The Falkland Islands Development Corporation, the archipelago's economic development agency, announced on Friday the appointment of Josh Smith as its new managing director, subject to final relocation arrangements. He will succeed Zachary Franklin, who will conclude his tenure in December.

item.title: MercoPress: Milei and Netanyahu discussed the Falklands in his only bilateral in New York
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for about twenty minutes on Thursday at United Nations headquarters, in what was his only bilateral meeting with a head of state or government during his trip to New York. Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno confirmed they discussed the Falklands.

item.title: MercoPress: “The UN has more reason to exist every day”, Uruguay's president said two days after Milei
item.description: Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi defended the United Nations' relevance and condemned the economic embargo on Cuba before the General Assembly on Thursday, in an address of just under twenty minutes that contrasted with that of his Argentine counterpart, Javier Milei, two days earlier from the same podium.

item.title: MercoPress: Poverty in Argentina rises to 32.3%, ending two years of decline
item.description: Poverty in Argentina reached 32.3% of people in the first half of 2026, an increase of 4.1 percentage points on the second half of 2025, the National Institute of Statistics and Census reported on Thursday. The figure interrupts the downward path the indicator had followed since mid-2024. Extreme poverty rose 1.2 points, from 6.3% to 7.5%.

item.title: MercoPress: Trump and Xi end the state visit with the trade truce extended and no substantive deals
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to Washington ended on Thursday with a two-month extension of the bilateral trade truce, agreed before the meeting itself, and no progress on the central issues dividing the two powers: tariffs, rare earths, agricultural purchases, Taiwan and export restrictions on advanced chips.

item.title: MercoPress: Nine days from the vote, neither Brazilian front-runner comes close to 50%
item.description: Neither of Brazil's two leading presidential candidates is approaching the threshold needed to win outright on October 4, according to the latest Datafolha poll, which puts President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on 40% of voting intentions and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro on 36%.

item.title: MercoPress: Netanyahu rejects genocide allegations before an assembly emptied by dozens of delegations
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday called genocide allegations against his country over the war in Gaza "the biggest lie of the century", in an address to the United Nations General Assembly that dozens of delegations left before he began speaking.

item.title: MercoPress: Punta Arenas/Falklands maritime links are based on history, economics and geography
item.description: The announced maritime and trade link between Punta Arenas in Chile and the Falkland Islands has been strongly argued and supported by the main newspaper from the Chilean austral city on the Magellan Strait and capital of the Magallanes Region.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Venezuela‘s interim president promises election after Maduro ousted
item.description: The opposition in Venezuela has slammed her for not setting even a tentative date for elections.

item.description: The BBC's Courtney Sargent explains how El Niño could have rapidly turned Hurricane Polo into one of the Pacific season's most powerful storms.

item.description: A report says the attacks, of which there have been at least 68, were not self-defence.

item.description: The suspects were flown to Miami to stand trial over the murder of Haitian President Jovenel Moise five years ago.

item.description: Mexicans celebrate the return of a centuries-old document that tells the story of the Aztec civilisation and its fall after the arrival of Spanish conquistadors.

item.description: A spotted wildcat long mistaken for relatives has been identified as a new species in Bolivia.

item.description: Thousands of turtles arrived at La Escobilla beach in Oaxaca within 48 hours, sanctuary officials said.

item.description: The burial site of the ancient pre-Incan Chimu culture was found largely intact.

item.description: Security camera footage shows a supermarket employee racing into action as a toddler runs towards moving traffic in Puebla, Mexico.
